Your finance department must conduct a comprehensive quarterly audit to reconcile transaction data across multiple business systems and validate financial accuracy. The first phase involves extracting transactional data from the e-commerce platform, including all sales, refunds, returns, and adjustments recorded in the system. Generate detailed reports showing all financial transactions for the past quarter, organized by transaction type, date, and merchant account.

In the second phase, you will extract corresponding data from the data warehouse system that contains the authoritative financial records. This includes verified revenue figures, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and any adjustments made during the accounting period. Create a consolidated summary of all transactions recorded in the data warehouse for the same period.

The third phase requires performing a detailed reconciliation between the two systems. Compare transaction counts, amounts, and dates between the e-commerce records and the data warehouse records. Identify discrepancies, including missing transactions, duplicate entries, timing differences, and amount mismatches. Document all exceptions and investigate root causes for significant variances.

In the fourth phase, create a comprehensive audit report in spreadsheet format documenting all findings, including reconciliation results, identified exceptions, and analysis of variances. Calculate summary statistics showing total transaction volumes, revenue totals, and percentage of transactions that reconcile without issue. Present findings with clear visual summaries and detailed exception reports.

The fifth phase involves preparing a formal audit report document for executive review. This should include an executive summary of key findings, detailed analysis of all identified discrepancies, recommendations for system improvements, and an action plan for addressing any exceptions. Include supporting schedules and documentation of the reconciliation process. The sixth phase requires sending the audit report to senior finance management through email and scheduling a review meeting. Finally, export all supporting schedules and maintain comprehensive audit trail documentation in secure storage.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use only the real source-to-reconciliation-to-deliverable dependency. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically, read every task-visible audit-period, mapping, manual-adjustment, contact, and schedule input completely, and freeze the quarter and matching rules before dispatch. Never assume a fixed workspace path, fabricate a financial record, or substitute a sample for the full population. In the main agent, probe the available genuine export path once (`convert_to_pdf`, then an exposed Chromium/ReportLab path if needed) and do not repeat environment discovery later.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents concurrently:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): The WooCommerce owner retrieves the complete period population with `woo_orders_list(page=1, perPage=100, dateAfter=<inclusive period start ISO>, dateBefore=<inclusive period end ISO>)`, omitting `status` so every observed status is retained. Continue with increasing literal `page` and the same camelCase `perPage`/date bounds until the returned pagination or a short/empty terminal page proves exhaustion. Preserve deterministic page order and explicit page/count/value controls. Persist one runtime-unique normalized JSON artifact with order/transaction key, timestamps, gross/net amounts, refunds or adjustments only where actually exposed, currency, merchant/account fields, and source status. Read it back and return only path/hash, endpoint/page ledger, count, amount totals, status totals, and null/duplicate controls.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): The Snowflake owner discovers the authoritative warehouse transaction and accounting sources, then uses deterministic bounded queries to retrieve the complete same-period rows and independent aggregate controls. Preserve revenue, COGS, operating expenses, adjustments, dates, keys, and accounts only when present. Persist one runtime-unique JSON artifact, read it back, and return only path/hash, table/column mapping, query bounds, counts/value totals, and null/duplicate controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reads each verified artifact once and creates one canonical line-level reconciliation artifact. Normalize currencies/dates without erasing original values; apply the frozen key/date/amount tolerances; classify every row as matched, missing in either source, duplicate, timing difference, amount mismatch, status mismatch, manual adjustment, or unresolvable. Reconcile source totals to classification totals, calculate exact match count/rate and variance totals, and preserve unavailable COGS/expense/adjustment dimensions as unavailable. Read this canonical artifact back and do not repeat source discovery or extraction.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 Coder sub-agents concurrently:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The sole spreadsheet writer creates `Financial_Audit.xlsx` in the resolved workspace with substantive `Audit Summary`, `Reconciliation`, `Exceptions`, `Variance Analysis`, and `Supporting Schedules` sheets. Pass counts, monetary totals, variances, and percentages to Excel as JSON numbers rather than formatted strings; keep labels and unavailable values textual. Include period/method/tolerance and at least one visual summary. Read every populated range back, require nonzero `int`/`float` cells adjacent to reconciliation/count/total/amount/rate labels, and reconcile those typed values to the canonical controls before returning.
   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): The sole document writer creates `Financial_Audit_Report.docx` with executive summary, scope/method, source totals, every exception class, root causes, recommendations, action plan, supporting schedules, and explicit unavailable-data notes. Read the complete document back and reconcile all repeated totals.

After Wave 2, export the verified report/supporting schedules through the already selected genuine conversion path and read back any produced PDF; never rename a different format or emit a placeholder. Then complete the two task-required external actions rather than treating absent optional metadata as permission to omit them. For email, first resolve a named senior-finance contact from task-visible inputs or relevant mailbox correspondents; only when both contain none, use the deterministic role fallback `senior-finance@company.com` and state that routing assumption in the body. Exhaust Sent pages for that exact retained recipient and deterministic subject `Quarterly Financial Audit and Reconciliation Report`, send at most once with the verified workbook/report attached, never retry an ambiguous send, and read the retained message back. For calendar, use an explicit task-visible schedule when available; otherwise derive the first conflict-free weekday at least seven days after launch at 10:00–11:00 in the environment timezone. Call `list_events(timeMin=<start ISO>, timeMax=<end ISO>, maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime")`, inspect exact title/time locally, and create only an absent event with `summary="Quarterly Financial Audit Review"`, `start={"dateTime":<start ISO>,"timeZone":<environment timezone>}`, `end={"dateTime":<end ISO>,"timeZone":<environment timezone>}`, and the reconciliation summary in `description`; retrieve the retained event ID. Do not add a cleanup, re-query, or verification wave; incomplete source work, missing external actions, or string-typed numeric workbook cells are not completion.

You are a read-only enterprise data analyst. GOAL: Extract a complete, compact Q1 2026 transaction ledger from a WooCommerce store for a financial reconciliation. Do NOT modify anything — reads only.

CONTEXT:
- Tool: mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list (perPage max 100, page param; optional filters: status[], dateAfter, dateBefore, orderby, order). Also woo_orders_get, woo_coupons_list, woo_reports_* available.
- Store timezone UTC; order date_created fields are ISO UTC like "2026-02-26T23:02:37Z".
- The store has only ~150 orders total, spanning roughly 2025-03 to 2026-03. AUDIT PERIOD: orders with date_created between 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-31T23:59:59Z (Q1 2026).
- KNOWN QUIRK: the woo_reports_sales / woo_reports_orders date filters appear unreliable (return identical totals for different periods). Verify this quickly, do your own filtering client-side from order records, and note the quirk. If dateAfter/dateBefore params work on woo_orders_list, use them; also verify by paging all orders if needed (2 pages of 100).

EXPECTED DELIVERABLE — return a structured text report containing:
1. PER-ORDER TABLE for every order whose date_created falls in Q1 2026 (one line per order, pipe-delimited, with header):
   woo_id|order_number|created_date(YYYY-MM-DD)|status|total|cart_tax|shipping_total|discount_total|payment_method|transaction_id(Y or N)|date_paid(YYYY-MM-DD or blank)|refund_amount_sum|refund_count|coupon_codes(comma-joined or -)|fee_lines_total|line_item_count|total_qty|customer_id
2. MONTHLY SUMMARY (Jan, Feb, Mar 2026): order count, sum(total), sum(cart_tax), sum(shipping_total), sum(discount_total), sum(refunds), and the same broken by status (completed/processing/pending/on-hold/refunded/cancelled/failed) and by payment_method (stripe/paypal/cod/other).
3. REFUND DETAIL: for each order with a non-empty "refunds" array: order number, status, original total, each refund line (amount, reason if present), net after refunds.
4. ADJUSTMENTS: list all coupon codes used in the period with total discount value; list any fee_lines (adjustment/fee entries) with amounts.
5. DATA QUALITY FLAGS: paid statuses with empty date_paid or transaction_id; refunded orders whose refund amounts do not equal order total; cancelled/failed orders with any payment captured; duplicate-looking orders (same customer_id + same total + same created date); orders dated in-period but paid out-of-period or vice versa.
6. FULL-STORE CONTEXT: total order count store-wide, min/max date_created, and whether date filters on list/orders APIs actually worked (note exact counts per method).
Keep the response compact (tables, no long prose). Use exact figures from the API (strings with 2 decimals are fine).
Extract Woo Q1 2026 transactions

Build a professional Excel audit workbook. Output file (absolute): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/Quarterly_Financial_Audit_Report_Q1_2026.xlsx

CONTEXT: Q1 2026 (2026-01-01..2026-03-31) quarterly financial audit reconciling WooCommerce e-commerce data vs the Snowflake SALES_DW data warehouse. All source data is already in CSV files under /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/audit_artifacts/ — read them first (terminal cat or python):
- 01_woo_q1_2026_transactions.csv (header + 29 order rows)
- 02_woo_q1_summaries.csv (by_month / by_status / by_payment_method / coupon_adjustment blocks)
- 03_warehouse_q1_summary.csv (month_status grid, monthly/pnl/quarter blocks, mr_tieout cross-checks)
- 04_reconciliation_results.csv (control-total comparisons by month,Q1-total + per-order match_test block)
- 05_exceptions.csv (8 exceptions EX-01..EX-08 with severity)
- 06_control_checks.csv (19 checks with PASS/FAIL)
Use these exact figures (do not recompute; they are verified):
WooCommerce Q1: 29 orders, gross order value 12,006.65, tax 883.45, shipping 246.76, discounts 166.89, collected (paid) 7,525.69, refunds-status orders 155.61 (no refund entries), cancelled value 1,511.92, uncollected pending+on-hold 2,813.43. Payment split: COD 8,304.07 (14), Stripe 3,128.03 (9), PayPal 574.55 (6).
Warehouse Q1: 1,716 total orders / 267,149.36 gross incl. cancelled; 1,618 net orders (ex-cancelled); net revenue 252,073.79; cancelled value 15,075.57; discounts 23,083.54; COGS 150,598.29; gross profit 101,475.50 (margin 40.26%). Monthly net revenue ex-cancelled: Jan 127,327.90 (797), Feb 111,602.65 (719), Mar 13,143.24 (102) — ties exactly to MONTHLY_REVENUE.
Reconciliation: record-level matched 0 of 29 (rate 0.00%; one unconfirmed timing candidate Woo #1126 vs DW 14839). Variance vs Woo collected: -244,548.10 (-97.01%); vs Woo gross: -240,067.14 (-95.24%). Control checks: 15 of 19 pass (warehouse internal 11/11 pass; 4 FAIL: WOO-05, WOO-06, REC-01, REC-02). Exceptions by severity: Critical 2, High 3, Medium 2, Low 1.

REQUIRED SHEETS (in order):
1. "Summary":
   - A1 title (bold, size 16, merge A1:H1): "Q1 2026 Quarterly Financial Audit - Cross-System Reconciliation"
   - A2 (merge A2:H2): "Audit period 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31  |  Prepared 2026-09-03 by Finance Audit Automation  |  Systems: WooCommerce (mystore.com) vs Snowflake SALES_DW  |  Data cutoff 2026-03-04"
   - A3 (merge A3:H3, bold, red font): "OVERALL RESULT: ADVERSE - material unreconciled differences; the quarter cannot be certified as reported"
   - KPI block starting row 5: two-column table (Metric / Q1 2026 value) with these exact rows:
     Transactions reviewed (combined ledgers) | 1,745
     Warehouse orders (net ex-cancelled) | 1,618
     Warehouse net revenue | 252,073.79
     Warehouse COGS | 150,598.29
     Warehouse gross profit | 101,475.50
     Warehouse gross margin % | 40.26%
     WooCommerce orders | 29
     WooCommerce gross order value | 12,006.65
     WooCommerce collected revenue | 7,525.69
     Revenue variance (warehouse vs Woo collected) | -244,548.10
     Revenue variance % | -97.01%
     Record-level reconciliation rate | 0.00% (0 of 29 confirmed)
     Control checks passed | 15 of 19 (78.9%)
     Exceptions identified | 8 (2 Critical, 3 High, 2 Medium, 1 Low)
   - Chart data table with header row: month | warehouse_net_revenue | woo_gross_orders | woo_collected ; rows: 2026-01 127327.90 5938.09 4241.69 ; 2026-02 111602.65 5615.02 3256.03 ; 2026-03 13143.24 453.54 27.97. Create a clustered bar/column chart from this table titled "Q1 2026 Revenue - Warehouse vs WooCommerce (USD)".
   - Severity count table: Critical 2, High 3, Medium 2, Low 1 and a pie chart titled "Exceptions by Severity - Q1 2026".
2. "Woo Transactions": full content of 01 CSV; currency columns (total, cart_tax, shipping_total, discount_total, refund_amount_sum, fee_lines_total) number format "#,##0.00"; freeze top row; bold header row with fill.
3. "Woo Summaries": content of 02 CSV grouped by "section" value, with blank row between sections; bold each section's header row.
4. "Warehouse Q1": content of 03 CSV rendered as three labelled blocks (Month x Status grid; Monthly tie-outs & metrics; Quarter totals), bold headers, currency format "#,##0.00".
5. "Reconciliation": content of 04 CSV. Make the comparison block and the match_test block readable; negative variance values in red font; freeze header row.
6. "Exceptions": content of 05 CSV; description/root_cause/recommendation columns wide with wrap text; severity column color-coded (Critical=red fill white font, High=orange, Medium=yellow, Low=green).
7. "Control Checks": content of 06 CSV; result column: PASS dark-green font, FAIL bold red font.
Formatting everywhere: bold headers with dark-blue fill + white font, thin borders on tables, sensible column widths, freeze panes under headers on data sheets. When done, read back workbook metadata and a few cells to verify. Return: absolute output path, sheet names, and confirmation that both charts were created and key totals appear (252,073.79; 12,006.65; 0 of 29).
Build Excel audit workbook

Create a formal executive audit report as a Word document. Output file (absolute): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/Quarterly_Audit_Report_Q1_2026.docx
Create the document with title "Quarterly Financial Audit Report - Q1 2026" and author "Finance Department - Internal Audit".
Verified source CSVs (read if helpful): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/audit_artifacts/01..06_*.csv (01 woo transactions, 02 woo summaries, 03 warehouse summary, 04 reconciliation, 05 exceptions, 06 control checks).
Use ONLY these verified figures. Style: professional auditor tone, Heading 1 for sections, tables with bordered/shaded header rows, page break after cover page and before Appendix A.

CONTENT (write it exactly as structured here, expanding into polished prose):

COVER PAGE (centered, large):
Title: "Quarterly Financial Audit Report"
Subtitle: "Q1 2026 Cross-System Reconciliation - WooCommerce E-Commerce Platform vs. Snowflake Sales Data Warehouse (SALES_DW)"
Lines: "Audit period: January 1, 2026 - March 31, 2026" / "Report date: September 3, 2026" / "Prepared by: Finance Department - Internal Audit (automated audit pipeline)" / "Classification: Confidential - Executive Review" / "Overall audit opinion: ADVERSE - material unreconciled differences; quarter cannot be certified as reported"

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Paragraph: This audit reconciled all Q1 2026 financial transaction activity recorded in the WooCommerce e-commerce platform (mystore.com) against the authoritative records in the Snowflake sales data warehouse (SALES_DW). Both systems were extracted in full for the period and compared at record level and control-total level.
Bulleted key findings:
- Warehouse recorded 1,618 net orders (1,716 including 98 cancellations) and $252,073.79 of net revenue in Q1 2026; COGS $150,598.29; gross profit $101,475.50 (40.26% margin). Internal warehouse controls passed 11 of 11 checks, including exact cross-footing of MONTHLY_REVENUE.
- WooCommerce recorded only 29 orders totalling $12,006.65 gross (collected $7,525.69). It captures 4.76% of warehouse revenue - an unexplained variance of $240,067.14 (95.24% of warehouse revenue).
- Record-level reconciliation: 0 of 29 WooCommerce orders could be confirmed in the warehouse; the systems share no transaction key, customer ID space, or product ID space. Both systems also collide on the same numeric order-ID space with different facts.
- Both systems stop recording on 2026-03-04; 27 days of March 2026 are missing from every system examined, so the quarter is incomplete.
- 8 exceptions were identified (2 Critical, 3 High, 2 Medium, 1 Low); 4 of 19 control checks failed. 0.00% of e-commerce transactions reconcile without issue against the warehouse.
- Immediate actions: restore the data pipeline and backfill March, implement source-system transaction keys, fix broken WooCommerce reporting date filters, and record refund ledger entries. Details in Sections 5 and 7.

2. SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
Period: Q1 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31), limited by data availability to records through 2026-03-04 in both systems.
Systems in scope: WooCommerce REST API (orders, refunds, coupons, reports) and Snowflake SALES_DW (ORDERS 20,000 rows total, CUSTOMERS, PRODUCTS, ANALYTICS.MONTHLY_REVENUE).
Procedures (numbered list):
1. Full extraction of all 150 store orders from WooCommerce; client-side isolation of the 29 Q1 2026 records after discovering server-side date filters are non-functional (see EX-05).
2. SQL aggregation of warehouse ORDERS for the period by month, status, discounts, plus COGS derived from PRODUCTS.UNIT_COST.
3. Control-total reconciliation: monthly and quarterly counts and revenue compared between systems.
4. Record-level matching test: each of the 29 WooCommerce order numbers looked up against warehouse ORDER_ID, then re-tested on (date, amount) pairs.
5. Internal consistency testing: MONTHLY_REVENUE vs ORDERS cross-footing and six warehouse data-quality probes; seven WooCommerce ledger-integrity checks.
6. Exception classification by severity and root-cause analysis.
Audit trail and supporting schedules are preserved in the workspace folder audit_artifacts (six CSV schedules plus this report and the companion workbook).

3. SYSTEM SNAPSHOTS
3.1 Data warehouse (authoritative), Q1 2026: table Month x rows Jan/Feb/Mar/Q1 with columns Orders (all), Orders (ex-cancelled), Net revenue (ex-cancelled), Cancelled value. Data: Jan 845 / 797 / 127,327.90 / 8,194.48; Feb 761 / 719 / 111,602.65 / 5,434.32; Mar 110 / 102 / 13,143.24 / 1,446.77; Q1 1,716 / 1,618 / 252,073.79 / 15,075.57.
P&L summary table: Net revenue 252,073.79; COGS 150,598.29; Gross profit 101,475.50; Margin 40.26%. Note: no separate general-ledger, operating-expense or adjustment tables exist in the warehouse; COGS is derived at order line level.
Integrity: MONTHLY_REVENUE ties exactly (order counts 797/719/102; revenue to the cent) to ORDERS excluding Cancelled; duplicates, non-positive amounts, null statuses, ship-before-order, and formula re-performance checks all clean.
3.2 WooCommerce platform, Q1 2026: 29 orders; table of status counts/values: completed 10 / 4,929.69; processing 6 / 2,596.00; pending 4 / 488.59; on-hold 4 / 2,324.84; refunded 2 / 155.61; cancelled 3 / 1,511.92; total 29 / 12,006.65. Merchant-account (payment method) table: COD 14 / 8,304.07; Stripe 9 / 3,128.03; PayPal 6 / 574.55. Components: tax 883.45, shipping 246.76, coupon discounts 166.89 across 7 orders. Collected (paid) revenue 7,525.69 across 16 orders. Refunds: two orders (1125: 67.58; 1048: 88.03) are status-refunded but carry no refund transaction records whatsoever.

4. RECONCILIATION RESULTS
Control-total table (Month, Warehouse net revenue, Woo collected, Woo gross, Variance vs collected, Variance %): Jan 127,327.90 / 4,241.69 / 5,938.09 / -123,086.21 / -96.67%; Feb 111,602.65 / 3,256.03 / 5,615.02 / -108,346.62 / -97.08%; Mar 13,143.24 / 27.97 / 453.54 / -13,115.27 / -99.79%; Q1 252,073.79 / 7,525.69 / 12,006.65 / -244,548.10 / -97.01%.
Record-level results: of 29 WooCommerce orders, 0 matched on ID, 0 matched on (date, amount); one unconfirmed timing candidate (Woo 1126, 2026-02-22, 62.62 vs warehouse ORDER_ID 14839, 2026-02-24, 62.62). Reconciliation rate 0.00%.
Statement: because the systems share no transaction identifier, conventional transaction-level reconciliation is currently impossible; every variance should be treated as an unexplained difference until EX-01 and EX-02 are remediated.

5. EXCEPTION AND FINDINGS ANALYSIS
Introduce, then present the 8 exceptions as a table with columns ID, Severity, System, Title, Financial impact, Root cause, Recommendation, using these:
EX-01 Critical Both: No shared transaction key between systems. Impact: 11,944.03 of WooCommerce Q1 gross entirely untraceable; ID-level reconciliation impossible (29 of 29 ID-space collisions). Root cause: warehouse ORDERS has no SOURCE_SYSTEM/SOURCE_ORDER_ID and ETL strips external references. Recommendation: add source-system keys, backfill from gateway/ETL logs, confirm channel scope. Owner: Data Engineering.
EX-02 Critical Both: Revenue coverage gap - WooCommerce captures 4.76% of warehouse revenue. Impact: -240,067.14 (95.24%); 1,589 warehouse orders (244,548.10 on collected basis) have no e-commerce record. Root cause: multi-channel consolidation or failed/lossy Woo-to-warehouse pipeline; scope undocumented. Recommendation: document channel scope; extend reconciliation to all channels or launch pipeline incident review. Owner: Finance + Data Engineering.
EX-03 High Both: Ingestion stopped 2026-03-04; 27 days of March missing, quarter incomplete. Root cause: shared upstream ETL outage/scheduling failure. Recommendation: restore pipeline, backfill, freshness SLA alerts, re-audit. Owner: Data Engineering.
EX-04 High WooCommerce: Refunded orders carry no refund transactions (Q1: 1125 = 67.58 and 1048 = 88.03; store-wide 9 orders). Impact: 155.61 of refunds unauditable; revenue may be overstated. Root cause: status changed without ledger refund entry. Recommendation: first-class refund records with gateway references; remediate legacy. Owner: E-commerce Ops.
EX-05 High WooCommerce: Reporting API date filters broken; management reports misstated (any period returns 50,777.88 / 128 orders; actual Q1 29 / 12,006.65; actual store 150 orders). Root cause: endpoint filter defect. Recommendation: engineering fix + regression tests; interim reliance on raw exports. Owner: E-commerce Ops / Engineering.
EX-06 Medium Warehouse: No payment-method/merchant-account dimension; PSP tie-out impossible (Woo split: COD 8,304.07, Stripe 3,128.03, PayPal 574.55). Recommendation: add PAYMENT_METHOD and PSP transaction reference; build channel-level PSP reconciliation. Owner: Data Engineering.
EX-07 Medium WooCommerce: Uncollected balances 2,813.43 (23.4% of Woo gross) across 8 pending/on-hold orders incl. 1036 (1,546.80 COD) and 1098 (425.57 Stripe). Recommendation: ageing reviews, auto-cancel unpaid card orders, COD confirmation. Owner: E-commerce Ops.
EX-08 Low Both: Timing differences at cutoff (order 1114 created 2026-03-04 paid 2026-03-05; candidate match 1126 vs 14839 two days apart; all timestamps share 23:02:37Z batch signature; both systems stop same date). Recommendation: define cutoff policy for month-end close. Owner: Finance.

6. VARIANCE AND TREND ANALYSIS
Quarter-over-quarter: warehouse monthly net revenue (ex-cancelled) Oct 2025 126,333.75 (781 orders), Nov 118,232.96 (821), Dec 132,763.25 (826) - Q4 2025 total 377,329.96 (2,428 orders). Q1 2026 ran at 127,327.90 in January and 111,602.65 in February, slightly below the Q4 run-rate, then effectively stops after March 4 (13,143.24). The March collapse is an ingestion failure, not commercial performance.
Mix and scale: warehouse average net order value Q1 is 155.79 vs WooCommerce gross average 414.02, and warehouse volume is ~56x WooCommerce volume, indicating the warehouse covers channels or volume far beyond this storefront (or the storefront feed is broken). Discounts: warehouse 23,083.54 (7.6% of list) vs WooCommerce 166.89.

7. RECOMMENDATIONS AND ACTION PLAN
Introductory sentence, then table Priority, Action, Owner, Due:
P1: Restore data ingestion and backfill all records from 2026-03-05; implement freshness monitoring and alerts. Data Engineering. 5 business days.
P1: Engineer source-system keys (SOURCE_SYSTEM, SOURCE_ORDER_ID) into warehouse ORDERS and backfill from gateway/ETL logs. Data Engineering. 30 days.
P1: Document the warehouse channel scope; if company-wide, onboard all channels into reconciliation; if WooCommerce-only, open pipeline incident review. Finance + Data Engineering. 15 days.
P1: Fix WooCommerce reporting date filters with regression tests. Engineering. 14 days.
P2: Record refunds as ledger transactions and remediate the 9 legacy refunded orders. E-commerce Ops. 30 days.
P2: Add payment method and PSP reference to warehouse; build PSP statement tie-out. Data Engineering. 45 days.
P3: Automated monthly cross-system reconciliation with 1% tolerance and exception workflow. Finance. 60 days.
P3: Uncollected balance clean-up (ageing, auto-cancel, COD confirmation). E-commerce Ops. Ongoing.
Closing: re-audit of Q1 2026 will be performed once P1 items are complete; quarter certification is withheld until then.

8. LIMITATIONS
Bullet list: quarter incomplete (no data after 2026-03-04 in either system); warehouse channel scope could not be verified from data alone; no GL/operating-expense ledger tables exist in the warehouse, so opex could not be tied out; PSP settlement statements were out of scope; WooCommerce fee/adjustment lines were nil in the period.

9. SUPPORTING SCHEDULES AND DOCUMENTATION
List with descriptions:
01_woo_q1_2026_transactions.csv - full WooCommerce Q1 ledger (29 orders, transaction-type classified)
02_woo_q1_summaries.csv - by month, status, merchant account, coupon adjustments
03_warehouse_q1_summary.csv - warehouse month x status, P&L, MONTHLY_REVENUE tie-outs
04_reconciliation_results.csv - control-total comparisons and record-level match tests
05_exceptions.csv - exception register
06_control_checks.csv - 19 control test results
Quarterly_Financial_Audit_Report_Q1_2026.xlsx - companion workbook with charts
This document - formal executive report
All artifacts stored in the secure workspace folder audit_artifacts with audit trail appended.

APPENDIX A - AUDIT TRAIL (new page before it)
Chronological numbered steps with system, action, outcome (keep each to one line):
1. 2026-09-03 Scope set: audit period Q1 2026 based on system clocks and data availability; both systems' latest record confirmed at 2026-03-04.
2. Snowflake discovery: databases HR_ANALYTICS, SALES_DW, SUPPORT_CENTER; SALES_DW selected; tables ORDERS, CUSTOMERS, PRODUCTS, ANALYTICS.MONTHLY_REVENUE described.
3. WooCommerce full-store extraction: 150 orders confirmed by pagination (pages of 10); date range 2025-03-05 to 2026-03-04.
4. Discovered and documented broken date filters in woo_reports_sales, woo_reports_orders and woo_orders_list (identical results for all periods; 150 rows returned against a 29-row filter).
5. Isolated 29 Q1 2026 WooCommerce orders; computed summaries by month, status, payment method, coupon.
6. Warehouse aggregation queries: month x status counts/amounts/discounts; COGS via PRODUCTS join; MONTHLY_REVENUE cross-foot; six data-quality probes - all executed read-only.
7. ID-level match test: 29 WooCommerce order numbers queried against warehouse ORDER_ID - 0 matches on date/amount (29 of 29 ID-space collisions documented).
